title: From chat to checkout: give your products a home online
excerpt: A practical guide to creating a storefront your customers can browse, shop and come back to.

children.text: Selling through social media brings customers into the conversation. Keeping product information and order records organised helps you manage what happens next.
Give customers somewhere to browse

You can keep sharing products on WhatsApp and Instagram while giving customers one place to see what is available. A storefront brings your product pictures, prices and descriptions together, so each conversation does not have to start from scratch.
Start with clear product information

Choose a small set of products to list first. Add accurate prices, useful descriptions and photographs that show what a customer will receive. If a product comes in different sizes or colours, make those choices clear and keep stock records up to date.
Walk through the experience as a customer. Look for missing information before you share your store.
Make the next step easy

Share your store link in your social profiles and with customers who ask for your catalogue. Check the store on your own phone before sharing it: can you find a product, understand the delivery options and follow the checkout steps?
Keep your daily work connected

Review orders and their payment status before preparing a delivery. Update fulfilment as an order moves forward, and use customer history when someone returns. A storefront is most useful when the records behind it stay organised.
